title: ANOR: Scaling Sparse Attention with a GPU-PNM Computing Hierarchy
summary: ANOR replaces PNM-centric sparse-attention execution, in which the near-memory device computes most of the attention and becomes the bottleneck, with a GPU-centric tiering scheme: the GPU serves attention from a cache of recently selected KV entries, the CXL-PNM device handles only cache misses, and a bounded update policy plus an Early Streaming Buffer limit link traffic and redundant DRAM reads. Its costs are the need for CXL-PNM hardware, added system complexity across two compute tiers, GPU memory reserved for the KV selection cache, and an adaptive cache-factor mechanism that trades hit ratio against batch size under varying load. It can fail if the workload lacks the selection locality the GPU cache depends on, if miss rates exceed what the low-bandwidth PNM tier can absorb, or if CXL link saturation negates the decoupling of cache updates from decode execution.
rationale: The technique requires CXL-attached processing-near-memory hardware that the reader does not possess and cannot provision on a single 24 GB GPU or through third-party APIs, so it is relevant to track but not adoptable or testable today.
technique: GPU-centric KV cache tiering over CXL-PNM

claims.statement: ANOR replaces PNM-centric sparse-attention execution, in which the near-memory device computes most of the attention and becomes the bottleneck, with a GPU-centric tiering scheme: the GPU serves attention from a cache of recently selected KV entries, the CXL-PNM device handles only cache misses, and a bounded update policy plus an Early Streaming Buffer limit link traffic and redundant DRAM reads. Its costs are the need for CXL-PNM hardware, added system complexity across two compute tiers, GPU memory reserved for the KV selection cache, and an adaptive cache-factor mechanism that trades hit ratio against batch size under varying load. It can fail if the workload lacks the selection locality the GPU cache depends on, if miss rates exceed what the low-bandwidth PNM tier can absorb, or if CXL link saturation negates the decoupling of cache updates from decode execution.
ANOR improves decode throughput by 2.3x over HiSparse and 2.0x over a PNM-centric baseline on average across two models and three long-context agentic workloads.
